The deadly triad: how a guess can train itself upward

Function approximation, bootstrapping and off-policy data each make RL practical. Off-policy value learners such as deep Q-networks (DQN) and soft actor-critic (SAC) use all three, even though together they can let a prediction feed its own target with nothing to pull it back down.

Learning from a fixed dataset: missing actions and bad demonstrations

A fixed robot dataset can mislead a learner in two different ways: a hole, where it asks about actions nobody tried, and mistakes, where it copies bad demonstrations. Stay close to the data for the first, and weight actions by the reward for the second.
